src.q: Each film-coated tablet contains 8 mg ondansetron (as ondansetron hydrochloride dihydrate).
Each tablet contains 38.274 mg of lactose.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Adults: nausea and vomiting from cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy; prevention of post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV). Established PONV: injection recommended.

src.q: Ondansetron is indicated for the management of nausea and vomiting induced by cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Ondansetron is indicated for the prevention of post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV).
For treatment of established PONV, administration by injection is recommended.

items.t: Children aged 6 months and over: chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. Oral ondansetron has not been studied for PONV in children (IV recommended).

src.q: Ondansetron is indicated for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) in children aged ≥6 months.
No studies have been conducted on the use of orally administered ondansetron in the prevention and treatment of PONV in children aged ≥1 month

items.t: Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy is outside the licensed indications (MHRA: second-line use in hyperemesis gravidarum only after full discussion of benefits and risks).

src.q: Outside of its authorised indications, ondansetron is also used second line for treating women with hyperemesis gravidarum
this decision should be made in consultation with the patient after she has been fully informed of the potential benefits and risks of the different treatment options

items.t: 8 mg 1-2 hours before chemotherapy or radiotherapy, then 8 mg every 12 hours for up to 5 days. Highly emetogenic chemotherapy: a single dose of up to 24 mg with dexamethasone 12 mg orally, 1-2 hours before.

src.q: The recommended oral dose is 8mg taken 1 to 2 hours before chemotherapy or radiation treatment, followed by 8 mg every 12 hours for a maximum of 5 days
For highly emetogenic chemotherapy a single dose of up to 24 mg ondansetron taken with 12 mg oral dexamethasone sodium phosphate, 1 to 2 hours before chemotherapy, may be used.

items.t: 16 mg one hour before anaesthesia.

src.q: The recommended oral dose is 16 mg taken one hour prior to anaesthesia.

items.t: Elderly and renal impairment: no change to oral dose. Moderate or severe hepatic impairment: maximum 8 mg per day.

src.q: Elderly No alteration of oral dose or frequency of administration is required.
In such patients a total daily dose of 8 mg should not be exceeded.

items.t: CINV, 6 months to 17 years: IV dose first (by BSA or weight), then oral dosing from 12 hours later for up to 5 days - BSA > 0.6 to ≤ 1.2 m²: 4 mg every 12 hours; > 1.2 m²: 8 mg every 12 hours; weight > 10 kg: 4 mg every 12 hours. Total daily dose must not exceed the adult dose of 32 mg.

src.q: Oral dosing can commence 12 hours later and may be continued for up to 5 days (Table 1). The total dose over 24 hours (given as divided doses) must not exceed adult dose of 32 mg.
> 1.2 m2 5 mg/m2 or 8 mg IV plus 8 mg syrup or tablet after 12 hours 8 mg syrup or tablet every 12 hours
> 10 kg Up to 3 doses of 0.15 mg/kg IV every 4 hours 4 mg syrup or tablet every 12 hours

items.t: Not licensed for CINV under 6 months; oral use for PONV in children not studied (IV recommended). Children on hepatotoxic chemotherapy: monitor liver function closely.

src.q: Ondansetron is indicated for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) in children aged ≥6 months.
Paediatric patients receiving ondansetron with hepatotoxic chemotherapeutic agents should be monitored closely for impaired hepatic function.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to ondansetron or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the ondansetron or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: With apomorphine (profound hypotension and loss of consciousness reported).

src.q: Concomitant use with apomorphine is contraindicated
Based on reports of profound hypotension and loss of consciousness when ondansetron was administered with apomorphine hydrochloride

items.t: Dose-dependent QT prolongation; torsade de pointes reported. Avoid in congenital long QT syndrome. Caution if QTc is or may become prolonged: electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure, bradyarrhythmias, or other QT-prolonging drugs. Correct hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia first.

src.q: Ondansetron prolongs the QT interval in a dose-dependent manner
Avoid ondansetron in patients with congenital long QT syndrome.
Ondansetron should be administered with caution to patients who have or may develop prolongation of QTc, including patients with electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure, bradyarrhythmias
Hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia should be corrected prior to ondansetron administration.

items.t: Serotonin syndrome reported with other serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs): if the combination is needed, observe the patient.

src.q: If concomitant treatment with ondansetron and other serotonergic drugs is clinically warranted, appropriate observation of the patient is advised.

items.t: Myocardial ischaemia reported (mostly with IV use): alert patients to the signs and symptoms.

src.q: Cases of myocardial ischemia have been reported in patients treated with ondansetron.
Patients should be alerted to the signs and symptoms of myocardial ischemia.

items.t: Increases large bowel transit time: monitor patients with signs of subacute intestinal obstruction.

src.q: As ondansetron is known to increase large bowel transit time, patients with signs of subacute intestinal obstruction should be monitored following administration.

items.t: Adenotonsillar surgery: may mask occult bleeding - follow carefully.

src.q: In patients with adenotonsillar surgery prevention of nausea and vomiting with ondansetron may mask occult bleeding. Therefore, such patients should be followed carefully after ondansetron.

items.t: Hypersensitivity has occurred in patients sensitive to other 5-HT3 antagonists.

src.q: Hypersensitivity reactions have been reported in patients who have exhibited hypersensitivity to other selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonists.

items.t: Contains lactose: hereditary galactose intolerance, lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: QT-prolonging drugs or drugs causing electrolyte disturbance: caution - additional QT prolongation. Cardiotoxic drugs (anthracyclines, trastuzumab), erythromycin, ketoconazole, amiodarone and beta-blockers (e.g. atenolol) may increase the risk of arrhythmias.

src.q: Caution should be exercised when ondansetron is coadministered with drugs that prolong the QT interval and/or cause electrolyte abnormalities.
antiarrhythmics (such as amiodarone) and beta blockers (such as atenolol or timolol) may increase the risk of arrhythmias

items.t: Serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs): serotonin syndrome reported; observe the patient if combined.

src.q: There have been post-marketing reports describing patients with serotonin syndrome (including altered mental status, autonomic instability and neuromuscular abnormalities) following the concomitant use of ondansetron and other serotonergic drugs (including SSRIs and SNRIs).

items.t: Apomorphine: contraindicated (profound hypotension, loss of consciousness).

src.q: concomitant use with apomorphine is contraindicated

items.t: Tramadol: ondansetron may reduce its analgesic effect.

src.q: Data from small studies indicate that ondansetron may reduce the analgesic effect of tramadol.

items.t: Potent CYP3A4 inducers (phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin) lower ondansetron levels. No interaction with alcohol, temazepam, furosemide, morphine or tramadol pharmacokinetics in studies.

src.q: In patients treated with potent inducers of CYP3A4 (i.e. phenytoin, carbamazepine, and rifampicin), the oral clearance of ondansetron was increased and ondansetron blood concentrations were decreased.
Specific studies have shown that there are no interactions when ondansetron is administered with alcohol, temazepam, furosemide, alfentanil, tramadol, morphine, lidocaine, propofol and thiopental.

items.t: No change in dose, frequency or route.

src.q: Patients with Renal Impairment No alteration of daily dosage or frequency of dosing, or route of administration are required.

items.t: Moderate or severe hepatic impairment: clearance much reduced and half-life prolonged - do not exceed 8 mg per day.

src.q: Clearance of ondansetron is significantly reduced and serum half-life significantly prolonged in subjects with moderate or severe impairment of hepatic function.
In such patients a total daily dose of 8 mg should not be exceeded.

items.t: SmPC: suspected to cause orofacial malformations with first-trimester use (about 3 extra oral clefts per 10,000 women treated); cardiac malformation data conflict. Should not be used in the first trimester.

src.q: ondansetron is suspected to cause orofacial malformations when administered during the first trimester of pregnancy
Ondansetron should not be used during the first trimester of pregnancy.

items.t: MHRA: small increased risk of cleft lip/palate after first-trimester use. If ondansetron is considered for severe pregnancy sickness, counsel the woman on benefits and risks and decide jointly.

src.q: use of ondansetron during the first trimester of pregnancy is associated with a small increased risk of the baby having a cleft lip and/or cleft palate
women must be counselled on the potential benefits and risks of use, both to her and to her unborn baby and the final decision should be made jointly

items.t: BUMPS (differs in emphasis): can be used for pregnancy sickness that stops normal life; birth-defect risks are very low; no concern about miscarriage, stillbirth, preterm birth or low birth weight.

src.q: Ondansetron can be used to treat pregnancy sickness that is stopping you from living your normal life.
It is clear that these risks are very low, and most babies exposed in the womb to ondansetron do not have these birth defects.

items.t: SmPC: passes into animal milk - mothers taking ondansetron should not breastfeed.

src.q: It is therefore recommended that mothers receiving ondansetron should not breast-feed their babies.

items.t: SPS (differs from SmPC): can be used with caution; monitor the infant for sedation, irritability, diarrhoea, constipation and urinary retention. Unlikely to pass into milk in significant amounts.

src.q: Ondansetron can be used with caution during breastfeeding, but monitoring is required.
As a precaution, monitor for sedation, irritability, diarrhoea, or constipation and urinary retention.

items.t: Women of childbearing potential should consider contraception. No human fertility data.

src.q: Women of childbearing potential should consider the use of contraception.
There is no information on the effects of ondansetron on human fertility.

items.t: Very common: headache. Common: warmth or flushing, constipation.

src.q: Very common: Headache.
Common: Sensation of warmth or flushing.
Common: Constipation .

items.t: Uncommon: seizures, movement disorders (extrapyramidal reactions), arrhythmias, chest pain, bradycardia, hypotension, hiccups, raised liver function tests.

src.q: Uncommon: Arrhythmias, chest pain with or without ST segment depression, bradycardia.

items.t: QTc prolongation including torsade de pointes (rare); myocardial ischaemia (frequency not known).

src.q: Rare: QTc prolongation (including Torsade de Pointes)
Not known: Myocardial ischemia*

items.t: Immediate hypersensitivity, sometimes severe, including anaphylaxis (rare).

src.q: Rare : Immediate hypersensitivity reactions sometimes severe, including anaphylaxis.

items.t: Seizures and extrapyramidal reactions (oculogyric crisis, dystonia) - uncommon.

src.q: Uncommon: Seizures, movement disorders (including extrapyramidal reactions (such as oculogyric crisis, dystonic reactions and dyskinesia)

items.t: Correct hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia before treatment.

src.q: Hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia should be corrected prior to ondansetron administration.

items.t: SPS: no monitoring needed for oral use without risk factors; with non-modifiable risk factors, monitor ECG, magnesium and potassium before and during IV or prolonged treatment.

src.q: No monitoring is required in the absence of risk factors or in oral use.
Monitor ECG, magnesium and potassium before and during intravenous or prolonged treatment in people with non-modifiable patient and medicine risk factors.

items.t: Observe for serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs; monitor for subacute intestinal obstruction; children on hepatotoxic chemotherapy: liver function.

src.q: appropriate observation of the patient is advised

src.q: The tablets should be swallowed whole with liquid.

items.t: Seek urgent help for chest pain or pressure (possible myocardial ischaemia), palpitations or fainting.

src.q: Patients should be alerted to the signs and symptoms of myocardial ischemia.

src.q: Women of childbearing potential should consider the use of contraception.
